rules: Import `ruststream::prelude::*` in a service, or the broker crate's own prelude, which re-exports it; the broker and the codec stay explicit choices.

The runtimes are cargo features of `ruststream` that add up: `tokio` (the default), `compio` and `embassy` for a device; an app picks its runner with `#[ruststream::app]` (tokio), `#[ruststream::app(runtime = compio, cores = n)]` or `#[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)]`, and a crate with `default-features = false` enables the runtime it uses, a broker crate on tokio enables `tokio`.

A compio service enables `ruststream` with the `compio` feature and `#[ruststream::app(runtime = compio, cores = n)]`: core 0 receives every subscription, `workers(n)` and `threads(n)` are placed across the cores, handler state and bodies are `Send` as on tokio, and `ruststream::testing::compio::TestApp` drives it on the test's own compio runtime.

A device with no heap enables `ruststream` with `default-features = false` and `embassy`, `memory`, `macros`, a slice codec (`postcard` or `json-core`) and a logger (`log` or `defmt`); the build then allocates nothing, and `tokio`, `json`, `cbor`, `msgpack` or any crate that turns `alloc` on make it the heap build throughout.

In the build without `alloc` name the codec at the mount (`b.with_codec(PostcardCodec)`, `.out_reply(policy).codec(PostcardCodec)`), keep a continuation within 128 bytes, treat `ctx.after(..)` as a `Result`, read failures as `async move |failures: &Failures| ..`, name a batch with `.batch::<N>()` up to 16 (its outcomes are `Outcomes<HandlerOutcome, N>`, its replies `Outcomes<Reply, N>`, and `.retry_capacity::<CAP>()` is at least `N`), and declare the local bus as a `static LocalMemoryBus`.

The framework reports nothing until the app selects a logger with `.logger(TracingLogger)` (feature `tracing`, on with tokio), `.logger(LogLogger)` or `.logger(DefmtLogger)` from `ruststream::diagnostics`; the selection is process-wide, and the level of the logger's backend silences a warning. A build without `alloc` has `LogLogger` and `DefmtLogger`; test it with the embedded `TestApp`, which follows the build, and install `assert_no_alloc::AllocDisabler` as the test binary's global allocator.

A device broker over a channel or a socket returns a `ReadyHint` from `Subscriber::ready_hint`, a handle on the state its stream reads that is `true` whenever the next poll could yield, so the embedded app skips the poll of an idle subscription; `harness::local_readiness` checks it.

Declare a handler as an `async fn` under `#[subscriber(..)]` whose first parameter is `&T` for one message or `&[T]` for a batch; mount it with `b.include(handler)` inside `with_broker`, whose closure takes the scope by value and returns the chain (`|b| b.include(a).include(b)`, `|b| b` for a publish-only broker), and a batch handler with `.batch(n)`; `|b| { b.include(h); }` does not compile.

Steps after an `include` (`.out_reply(..)`, `.out(Marker, ..)`, `.out_retry(..)`, `.transform(..)`, `.max_attempts(..)`, `.dead_letter(..)`) belong to that include and need no terminal call; scope steps (`after_startup`, `include_router`) are written before the `include`s.

A reply type derives `Outgoing`: `#[outgoing(name = "..")]` fixes its destination and the subscriber writes the bare `reply`; a type with no name takes `reply("dest")` at the mount site (a declared name wins, and startup warns).
Publish from inside a handler through an `Out(out): Out<impl Publisher>` parameter bound at the mount site with `.out(marker, policy)`; a handler signature never names a broker's publisher type.

A publish a broker refuses returns the message wherever the broker's client did not take the payload: a handler's own `out.message(..).publish().await` error holds it (`PublishError::unsent()`, `None` where a `Take` publisher consumed the buffer), and another `Out` republishes it as it was.

The codec is chosen at the mount site (`with_broker_codec`, `Router::with_codec`, `.out_reply(policy).codec(..)`), never per message type; a type that is its own encoding derives `Serialized` or `Deserialized` and needs no codec; a codec of your own declares `type Frame<'a> = ();` and a `frame` returning `Ok(())` unless its frame names records.

A value a broker's delivery already holds (a row a driver read) reaches a handler as `&T`, or `&[T]` for a batch, once the broker crate's derive puts `T` on that lane; the type derives `Clone`, not `Deserialize`.

Several message types on one subscription are an enum deriving `InMessages`, one model per variant, used as the handler's input; pick the variant with `#[in_messages(header = "..")]` and `#[in_messages(value = "..")]` per variant, or `discriminate = path` for a rule a header cannot state, or `by_codec` for a rule only the decode codec can answer (the codec implements `FrameNames` for each model), and never with `#[serde(tag)]`.
A batch of carried values mounts with no reply and no `Out` slots, and a test asserts carried values with `with_value` and `received_values`, not `with`.
Cap redeliveries at the mount site with `.max_attempts(n)` and `.dead_letter(name)` right after `include`; `.out_retry(policy)` only replaces the publisher the retry copy leaves through.

Test a service by handing its production app to `ruststream::testing::TestApp::start` and address a broker by its production type, `tb.broker::<KafkaBroker>()`; do not mock the broker traits or build a second app for tests.
A broker crate's `testing` feature runs each broker in process under `TestApp::start`; `TestApp::start_live` runs the same test body against a running stand.

To act at the moment a subscription is called or a message is published, register `on_call` on `tb.broker::<B>().subscriber(name)` or `on_publish` on `published::<T>(name)` with an `async move |handle|` closure; never sleep for a window and read the record afterwards.

To react when a publish the runtime makes for a handler fails (a `retry_after` copy, a dead-letter copy, an `out_reply` reply), chain `.error(async move |failures: Failures| ..)` on the returned `HandlerOutcome`, or `ctx.after(outcome).error(..)` from the context; each `Failed` holds the cause and the message the runtime tried to send, a failed reply is acknowledged and the handler never runs again for it, a `.then` beside it runs only when the publish succeeded, a single outcome for a batch runs it once with every failed element in `Failures`, and without `.error` the loss is logged.

Inside `.error`, `failed.error()` is the cause: the publisher's own error when the publisher failed, which you downcast to the broker's error type to tell a transient failure (a refused connection) from a permanent one (a rejected message), the encode error (such as the codec's `CodecError`) for a reply that failed to encode, or `NoFreeRecordError` for a delayed retry copy whose store is full on the embedded runtime; on a subscription whose source declares `BrokerMoves` the runtime publishes no copy, so `.error` never runs and a warning names the subscription.
Generate `main` with `#[ruststream::app]` and run the service with `cargo run -- run`; use `start()` only when the service runs beside another server such as an HTTP framework.
Give a handler that computes its own threads with `threads(n)` (or `threads(n, by_key)`) instead of `spawn_blocking` or `rayon` inside it; keep `workers(n)` for I/O-bound concurrency.

A `threads(n)` handler's leftovers (spawned tasks, `and_after`, `after(..)`, `retry_after` timers) stay on its thread; it sends work to the app's runtime only through `spawn` or `run` on `Ctx<MainRuntime>`.
Size the app's runtime for I/O with `#[ruststream::app(flavor = "current_thread")]` or `worker_threads = n` when the computing handlers run on `threads(n)`.
To find the handlers that belong on `threads(n)`, turn on the `poll-diagnostics` feature: every subscription samples its handler's time in `poll` and warns past the threshold.

Tune poll diagnostics with `RustStream::poll_diagnostics(PollDiagnostics::new().threshold(..).sample_every(..))` before `with_broker`; export them with `Metrics::observe_poll_diagnostics` or `Otel::observe_poll_diagnostics`.
Broker-specific settings live on the broker crate's subscription descriptor and publish policy, in that crate's vocabulary; the core exposes none.

A broker crate's own mount step is an extension trait bounded on `IntoDeclared<Mk>` (or on `SubscriberBuilder<Def, MySource, ..>` when it follows the source) and reads the subscription's concurrency, batch size and name off the settings builder (`dispatch()`, `batch_size()`, `subscription_name()`) instead of a setting of its own that repeats `workers(n)`, `threads(n)` or `batch(n)`; a handler used outside any mount names its state, `handler::<()>`.

A broker crate implements one `Subscriber`, `Publisher` and set of capability traits for every runtime, and its delivery implements `IncomingMessage` (the accessors, no `Send` supertrait) and `Settle` (`ack`, `nack`, `nack_after`): their futures ask for `Send` when `tokio` or `compio` is on and for nothing on the embedded runner alone, so a client that holds `Rc` or `RefCell` serves the embedded runner and does not compile next to `tokio`.

A broker crate depends on `ruststream = { version = "0.8", default-features = false, features = ["tokio"] }` and lists the facade's `conformance` and `testing` features in its dev-dependencies; start from the rustdoc of the `Broker` trait, which orders the contract step by step.

`Publisher::publish` returns `PublishOutcome<'msg, Error, Form>`: a refused publish hands the unsent message back with `PublishMessageError::with_message`, or converts the bare error with `.into()` or `?` when the client consumed the buffer, and `lifecycle::refused_publish_returns_message` holds the broker to its `Unsent` declaration.

A broker's `BatchSubscriber::Batch` is a `BatchSlot` (a `Vec` of deliveries is one) and `batches(size)` returns a `BatchStream` whose `poll_fill` fills the slot the runtime lends; the runtime takes each batch out with `BatchSlot::hand_over`, which trades storage so no delivery is copied.

Use `ruststream-sqlx` for a transactional outbox over any RustStream broker and for task queues in the service's own Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB or SQLite tables; its docs.rs overview at https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx is the guide.

A transform that names a destination per delivery reads the address with `HeaderMap::get_shared` and passes the `Str` to `Outgoing::set_name`, so the name shares the delivery's buffer instead of being copied out of it.
Misuse is rejected at compile time by design: read the compiler error, it names the missing derive, the unbound slot or the wrong position; do not work around it with runtime checks.

Check what a change costs per message with `just bench --baseline=main`: it counts instructions and allocations per delivery on the core's own scenarios, and its numbers are the ones a pull request cites.
`just bench --baseline=main` fails on more than two percent more instructions, or on an allocation above a scenario's declared floor.
Open a pull request as a draft and leave it a draft until the maintainer marks it ready for review: CI runs nothing on a draft, so its time is spent once, on the work the maintainer wants checked.
